entries.opening: A mote of dust is the records’ smallest visible unit for expressing minuteness and for staging the claim that an entire teaching-world can appear within the least particle.
entries.zenBend: Masters contrast dust-fine smallness with all-encompassing scope: a staff enters it, a turning teaching fills it, and a scripture issues from one mote.
entries.scopeLimit: The entry does not make every compound containing “dust” a separate sense.

entries.opening: The incense table is the small furnishing beside the teaching seat that Feiyin Tongrong, Baichi Yuanshuo, and other named speakers strike to make an immediately audible point.
entries.zenBend: Formal addresses repeatedly pair raising the whisk with striking the table and asking whether the assembly hears; monastic rules also list the furnishing in public ceremony.
entries.scopeLimit: The object is not defined as a symbol; the stored cases show its furnishing and demonstrative uses.

entries.opening: The summer residence period is the formally bounded communal stay marked by entering, completing, and speaking at the summer assembly.
entries.zenBend: Zen masters use its opening and close as public occasions, while also testing whether merely passing the season settles the matter addressed to the assembly.
entries.scopeLimit: The term names the institutional summer period, not a private exercise.

entries.preferredTarget: the fragrant wind comes from the south
aliases: a fragrant wind comes from the south
entries.opening: The fragrant wind coming from the south is the first line of a paired answer whose cool palace-halls became a repeatedly raised Zen case phrase.
entries.zenBend: Yuanwu gives the couplet in answer to where the awakened ones emerge; Dahui’s break-through at hearing it and later masters’ quotation, challenge, and reuse keep it inside public case work.
entries.scopeLimit: The line retains its weather image; the entry does not assign wind or fragrance a free-standing symbolic code.

entries.opening: The group leader is the senior member who stands at the head of a visiting or junior group and leads its formal movements and responses.
entries.zenBend: Monastic rules assign this person the lead in lineup and lodging procedures; encounter records also identify the first participant by this office when the group enters a public exchange.
entries.scopeLimit: The title is a public group office, not a claim that its holder is the teaching authority.
